hook: The bill had a **service charge** I never agreed to.
hook_q: Can a restaurant force me to pay it?

slides.title: Short answer: **no.**
slides.body: No hotel or restaurant can force you to pay a service charge. It must tell you clearly that service charge is voluntary, optional and at your discretion.

slides.title: What restaurants **cannot do.**
list: Add it to the bill automatically or by default
Collect it under any other name
Refuse entry or service if you don't pay it
Add it to the food bill and charge GST on the total

slides.title: Issued under the **Consumer Protection Act.**
slides.body: The Central Consumer Protection Authority issued these guidelines under its power to prevent unfair trade practices.

slides.title: Upheld by the **Delhi High Court.**
slides.body: On 28 March 2025, a single judge of the Delhi High Court held that service charge is a voluntary payment and cannot be compulsory, and upheld the CCPA guidelines.

slides.title: Charged anyway? **Here's what to do.**
list: Ask the restaurant to remove it from the bill
File with the Consumer Commission on e-jagriti.gov.in
Complain to the District Collector or com-ccpa@nic.in

sources: CCPA Guidelines to prevent unfair trade practices and protection of consumer interest with regard to levy of service charge in hotels and restaurants, 4 July 2022 (consumeraffairs.nic.in)
Delhi High Court – National Restaurant Association of India v. Union of India, W.P.(C) 10683/2022, 28 March 2025 (delhihighcourt.nic.in)
caption:
Service charge on your restaurant bill? You don't have to pay it. 👇

1️⃣ No restaurant can force you to pay a service charge. It is voluntary and optional
2️⃣ It can't be added to the bill automatically or by default
3️⃣ It can't be collected under any other name
4️⃣ You can't be refused entry or service for not paying it
5️⃣ In March 2025, the Delhi High Court upheld the CCPA guidelines
6️⃣ Charged anyway? Ask for it to be removed, or call the National Consumer Helpline on 1915

Source: CCPA Guidelines on service charge, 4 July 2022; Consumer Protection Act, 2019 (Sec 18(2)(l))
